the higher mortality risk among blacks compared with that among whites is likely to be multifactorial and that further studies are needed to identify the specific factors that contribute to this risk.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher mortality after allogeneic transplantation for blacks might be related in part to genetic factors, but the possibility that sociocultural factors also contribute cannot be excluded.

race or ethnicity was associated with survival only among patients who underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
race or ethnicity is a strong and independent predictor of mortality after allogeneic transplantation.
race is a significant risk factor for mortality among patients who have allogeneic HCT.
race/ethnicity is an important factor that influences outcomes after SCT, and that the effect of race/ethnicity may differ according to the type of SCT.
